arxiv-2004-12406.title: Masking as an Efficient Alternative to Finetuning for Pretrained Language Models
arxiv-2004-12406.creator: Mengjie Zhao, Tao Lin, Fei Mi, Martin Jaggi, Hinrich Schütze
arxiv-2004-12406.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Mengjie Zhao, Tao Lin, Fei Mi, Martin Jaggi, Hinrich Schütze. We present an efficient method of utilizing pretrained language models, where we learn selective binary masks for pretrained weights in lieu of modifying them through finetuning. Extensive evaluations of masking BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT on eleven diverse NLP tasks show that our masking scheme yields performance comparable to finetuning, yet has a much smaller memory footprint when several tasks need to be inferred.

arxiv-2205-04121.title: Identifying Fixation and Saccades in Virtual Reality
arxiv-2205-04121.creator: Xiao-lin Chen a, c and Wen-jun Hou b,c
arxiv-2205-04121.description: Abstract Gaze recognition can significantly reduce the amount of eye movement data for a better understanding of cognitive and visual processing. Gaze recognition is an essential precondition for eye-based interaction applications in virtual reality. However, the three-dimensional characteristics of virtual reality environments also pose new challenges to existing recognition algorithms.

arxiv-2212-04370.title: Thin film epitaxial [111] Co 50 Pt 50 : Structure, magnetisation, and spin polarisation
arxiv-2212-04370.creator: N. Satchell, S. Gupta, M. Maheshwari, P. M. Shepley, M. Rogers, O. Cespedes, G. Burnell
arxiv-2212-04370.description: Abstract Ferromagnetic films with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy are of interest in spintronics and superconducting spintronics. Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy can be achieved in thin ferromagnetic multilayer structures, when the anisotropy is driven by carefully engineered interfaces. Devices with multiple interfaces are disadvantageous for our application in superconducting spintronics, where the current perpendicular to plane is affected by the interfaces.

arxiv-2303-07369.creator: S. Saracino, T. Shenar, S. Kamann, N. Bastian, M. Gieles, C. Usher, J. Bodensteiner, A. Kochoska, J. A. Orosz, H. Sana

arxiv-2404-16576.title: Implicit-Explicit schemes for decoupling multicontinuum problems in porous media
arxiv-2404-16576.creator: Maria Vasilyeva
arxiv-2404-16576.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Maria Vasilyeva. In this work, we present an efficient way to decouple the multicontinuum problems. To construct decoupled schemes, we propose Implicit-Explicit time approximation in general form and study them for the fine-scale and coarse-scale space approximations. We use a finite-volume method for fine-scale approximation, and the nonlocal multicontinuum (NLMC) method is used to construct an accurate and physically meaningful coarse-scale approximation. The NLMC method is an accurate technique to develop a physically meaningful coarse scale model based on defining the macroscale variables.

arxiv-2410-06026.title: Content-based Wake-up for Energy-efficient and Timely Top- k k IoT Sensing Data Retrieval
arxiv-2410-06026.creator: Junya Shiraishi, Anders E. Kalør, Israel Leyva-Mayorga, Federico Chiariotti, Petar Popovski, and Hiroyuki Yomo
arxiv-2410-06026.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Junya Shiraishi, Anders E. Kalør, Israel Leyva-Mayorga, Federico Chiariotti, Petar Popovski, and Hiroyuki Yomo. Energy efficiency and information freshness are key requirements for sensor nodes serving Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) applications, where a sink node collects informative and fresh data before a deadline, e.g., to control an external actuator. Content-based wake-up (CoWu) activates a subset of nodes that hold data relevant for the sink’s goal, thereby offering an energy-efficient way to attain objectives related to information freshness.

arxiv-2410-24066.title: Cough-E: A multimodal, privacy-preserving cough detection algorithm for the edge
arxiv-2410-24066.creator: Stefano Albini, Lara Orlandic, Jonathan Dan, Jérôme Thevenot, Tomas Teijeiro, Denisa‑Andreea Constantinescu, David Atienza
arxiv-2410-24066.description: Abstract Continuous cough monitors can greatly benefit doctors for home monitoring and treatment of respiratory diseases. Although many works propose algorithms to automate this task, they are still limited in terms of poor data privacy and short-term monitoring. Edge-AI is a promising paradigm to overcome these limitations by processing privacy-sensitive data close to their source.

arxiv-2505-17782.title: Thalia: A Global, Multi-Modal Dataset for Volcanic Activity Monitoring
arxiv-2505-17782.creator: Nikolas Papadopoulos, Nikolaos Ioannis Bountos, Maria Sdraka, Andreas Karavias, Gustau Camps-Valls, Ioannis Papoutsis
arxiv-2505-17782.description: Abstract Monitoring volcanic activity is of paramount importance to safeguarding lives, infrastructure, and ecosystems. However, only a small fraction of known volcanoes are continuously monitored. Satellite-based Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) enables systematic, global-scale deformation monitoring. However, its complex data challenge traditional remote sensing methods.

arxiv-2506-05203.title: Trustworthiness Preservation by Copies of Machine Learning Systems
arxiv-2506-05203.creator: Leonardo Ceragioli, Giuseppe Primiero
arxiv-2506-05203.description: Abstract A common practice of ML systems development concerns the training of the same model under different data sets, and the use of the same (training and test) sets for different learning models. The first case is a desirable practice for identifying high quality and unbiased training conditions.

arxiv-2507-08212.title: EvA: Evolutionary Attacks on Graphs
arxiv-2507-08212.creator: Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Soroush H. Zargarbashi, Jimin Cao, Aleksandar Bojchevski
arxiv-2507-08212.description: Abstract Even a slight perturbation in the graph structure can cause a significant drop in the accuracy of graph neural networks (GNNs). Most existing attacks leverage gradient information to perturb edges. This relaxes the attack’s optimization problem from a discrete to a continuous space, resulting in solutions far from optimal.

arxiv-2512-19894.creator: Kostas Karagiannis, Aristides Kontogeorgis, Konstantia Manousou Sotiropoulou

pmc-10574672.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Chamaenerion angustifolium (L.) Scop. is one of the promising sources of biologically active compounds and a valuable industrial crop. Recently, green extraction methods have become more topical. One of them is the application of deep eutectic solvents (DESs). pmc-10622946.title: Intracellular Plasmodium aquaporin 2 is important for sporozoite production in the mosquito vector and malaria transmission
pmc-10622946.creator: Alexander J. Bailey, Chiamaka Valerie Ukegbu, Maria Giorgalli, Tanguy Rene Balthazar Besson, George K. Christophides, Dina Vlachou
pmc-10622946.description: SignificanceThe results reported here uncover a uniquely evolved aquaporin in malaria parasites, which is important for production of sporozoites during the mosquito phase of the parasite lifecycle. Sporozoites are the parasite form responsible for malaria transmission to humans following a mosquito bite. Aquaporins are known transporters of water and other molecules across biological membranes.

pmc-10638390.title: Biosynthesis of barley wax β-diketones: a type-III polyketide synthase condensing two fatty acyl units
pmc-10638390.creator: Yulin Sun, Alberto Ruiz Orduna, Zhonghang Zhang, Sarah J Feakins, Reinhard Jetter
pmc-10638390.description: The surface coatings of cereal plants are dominated by waxy β-diketones crucial for drought resistance and, therefore, grain yield. Here, barley (Hordeum vulgare) wax analyses reveal β-diketone and associated 2-alkanol ester profiles suggesting a common C16 3-ketoacid precursor. Isotope analysis further shows that the major (C31) diketone is synthesized from two plastidial C16 acyl units.

pmc-11604763.title: Occurrence of selected Covid-19 drugs in surface water resources: a review of their sources, pathways, receptors, fate, ecotoxicity, and possible interactions with heavy metals in aquatic ecosystems
pmc-11604763.creator: S. R. Maremane, G. N. Belle, P. J. Oberholster, E. O. Omotola
pmc-11604763.description: The outbreak of the coronavirus disease 2019 (Covid-19) led to the high consumption of antibiotics such as azithromycin as well as corticosteroids such as prednisone, prednisolone, and dexamethasone used to treat the disease. Seemingly, the concentrations of these four Covid-19 drugs increased in wastewater effluents and surface water resources.

pmc-12409417.title: Neural interaction explainable AI predicts drug response across cancers
pmc-12409417.creator: Philipp Keyl, Julius Keyl, Andreas Mock, Gabriel Dernbach, Liliana H Mochmann, Niklas Kiermeyer, Philipp Jurmeister, Michael Bockmayr, Roland F Schwarz, Grégoire Montavon, Klaus-Robert Müller, Frederick Klauschen
pmc-12409417.description: Personalized treatment selection is crucial for cancer patients due to the high variability in drug response. While actionable mutations can increasingly inform treatment decisions, most therapies still rely on population-based approaches. Here, we introduce neural interaction explainable AI (NeurixAI), an explainable and highly scalable deep learning framework that models drug–gene interactions and identifies transcriptomic patterns linked with drug response.

pmc-12451809.title: Computerized decision support for antimicrobial prescribing: what every antibiotic steward should know
pmc-12451809.creator: Davide Bosetti, Rebecca Grant, Gaud Catho
pmc-12451809.description: Objective:To examine the potential role of computerized clinical decision support systems (CDSS) in antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and to identify significant challenges concerning their effectiveness and implementation.Design:Narrative review.Setting and methods:This review is based on existing literature regarding CDSS in AMS across various healthcare environments, such as hospitals and primary care facilities.

pmc-12618787.title: Immunotherapeutics in metastatic cancer management
pmc-12618787.creator: Manisha Shukla, Poorna Shri, Sunil Kumar Mahobiya, Rohit Kumar Vishwakarma
pmc-12618787.description: Metastatic cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely owing to the limitations of conventional treatments such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and targeted agents that are challenged by tumor heterogeneity, acquired resistance, and systemic toxicity. In contrast, immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative modality, harnessing the power of the immune system to selectively target and eradicate tumor cells.

pmc-12730153.title: Rapid Improvement of Refractory Cutaneous Hypereosinophilic Syndrome with Abrocitinib Plus Methylprednisolone: A Case Report
pmc-12730153.creator: Bei Liao, Xinze Li, Qianjie Qiu, Jing Zhang, Meiqin Xu, Xiaobing Wang, Weijun Liu, Ruijie Long
pmc-12730153.description: Hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) is a rare disorder characterized by persistent eosinophilia and end-organ damage. Cutaneous manifestations are frequently refractory to conventional therapies, including corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, creating a significant clinical challenge. The Janus kinase (JAK)-STAT pathway has been implicated in eosinophil activation and survival, suggesting a potential role for JAK inhibitors in management.

pmc-12985803.title: Subsequent Pregnancies After Conservative Placenta Accreta Management: Recurrent Accreta and Preserved Fertility, a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12985803.creator: Shmuel Somer, Doron Kabiri, Lauren H. Yaeger, Shmuel Herzberg, Yossef Ezra, Aharon Tevet, Joshua I. Rosenbloom
pmc-12985803.description: Background: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is a serious obstetric condition characterized by abnormal placental adherence to the uterus that can lead to major maternal morbidity. While hysterectomy has traditionally been the standard management, uterus-preserving approaches are increasingly used to preserve fertility. The risk of recurrent PAS in subsequent pregnancies and the overall fertility outcomes following conservative management remain unclear.

pmc-13003047.title: Nervous necrosis virus capsid protein functions as a SUMO E3 ligase to activate MAVS-dependent NF-κB signaling
pmc-13003047.creator: Wanwan Zhang, Xiaoqi Chen, Bingbing Sun, Lan Yao, Xingchen Xiong, Meisheng Yi, Kuntong Jia
pmc-13003047.description: Nervous necrosis virus (NNV) is a lethal aquatic pathogen that activates NF-κB signaling to manipulate host immune responses, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the NNV capsid protein (CP) as a novel viral SUMO E3 ligase that promotes SUMOylation of Lateolabrax japonicus mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS) to drive NF-κB activation.

pmc-13019192.title: One-Step Rh-Catalyzed Atom-Economical Cyclization of Acetophenones and Methyl Propiolate Affording Isoquinoline Derivatives
pmc-13019192.creator: Fanjia Zeng, Yulin Cai, Yibiao Xiao, Huawu Xu, Yixia Hong, Junyan Gao, Jiezhuang Fang, Qingqiang Zeng, Xianzhe Su
pmc-13019192.description: Isoquinoline derivatives hold significant importance in the fields of natural product chemistry, medicinal chemistry, and biological sciences. Currently, researchers are actively exploring efficient and general synthetic methodologies for these compounds. Herein, we report the use of hydroxylamine-O-sulfonic acid (HOSA) as a novel transient directing group (TDG) to enable the selective ortho–C-H functionalization/cyclization of acetophenones with methyl propiolate.

pmc-13405852.title: A Torilis japonica Extract–GHK-Cu Complex Attenuates Th2 Cytokines and Promotes Keratinocyte Recovery: A Potential Antioxidant Strategy for Atopic Dermatitis
pmc-13405852.creator: Soojin Jeon, Jihye Maeng, Jiwon Lee, Young-Min Kim, Gaewon Nam
pmc-13405852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic skin disorder driven by Th2 immune dysregulation, persistent inflammation, and epidermal barrier defects. Oxidative stress acts as a major upstream factor in this process, amplifying inflammatory signals and worsening disease severity. While current treatments relieve acute symptoms, long-term application is often constrained by side effects and poor barrier restoration, pointing to a need for safer, multifaceted alternatives.

pmc-13429605.title: Quantification of [11C]CURB PET using an irreversible reference tissue model with a cluster-derived pseudo-reference region
pmc-13429605.creator: Lucas Narciso, Shahtaj S. Dheda, Raesham Mahmood, Rachel F. Tyndale, Tina McCluskey, Jerry Warsh, Bernard Le Foll, Kimberly L. Desmond, Stefan Kloiber, Isabelle Boileau
pmc-13429605.description: IntroductionQuantification of [11C]CURB, an irreversible positron emission tomography (PET) radiopharmaceutical used to image fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), requires invasive arterial sampling. Developing a non-invasive approach for [11C]CURB is challenging, since traditional reference region models are not directly applicable and the ubiquitous brain expression of FAAH complicates the identification of a ligand-free reference region.

pmc-13445319.title: Janus Nanostructures Enabled by Confined Interfacial Engineering for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response
pmc-13445319.creator: Limeng Song, Cheng Song, Feiyue Hu, Yongqiang Chen, Linan Wang, Huagao Wang, Li Guan, Duo Chen, Kesong Yu, Yabo Huang, Shihao Jia, Xin Xu, Qiancheng Gao, Dou Zhang, Hailong Wang, Haijiao Xie, Rui Zhang, Bingbing Fan
pmc-13445319.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Regulating electromagnetic responses through interfacial design has attracted increasing attention, while the precise construction and mechanism understanding of asymmetric nano‐interfaces remain largely unexplored, particularly at the nanoscale. Herein, taking a representative carbon‐based microwave absorber as a model system, we develop a confined diffusion‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy to construct SiC@C Janus hollow nanostructures with well‐defined asymmetric nano‐interfaces, enabling the coordinated regulation of interfacial configuration and electromagnetic functionality.

pmc-13500737.title: 泛素化修饰调控T细胞稳态与自身免疫病
pmc-13500737.creator: 梦迪 张, 明久 赵, 佳琦 黄, 智广 周, 斌 赵
pmc-13500737.description: 泛素化是一种高度动态且可逆的翻译后修饰，广泛参与真核细胞内蛋白质降解、信号转导及细胞功能调控。泛素化修饰通过泛素活化酶(ubiquitin-activating enzyme，E1)-泛素缀合酶(ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme，E2)-泛素-蛋白质连接酶(ubiquitin-protein ligase，E3)三级酶系协同作用，将泛素以不同链型连接于底物蛋白，从而决定底物蛋白的蛋白酶体降解、亚细胞转运及非降解性支架功能。在免疫系统中，E3与去泛素化酶(deubiquitinases，DUB)通过调控底物选择和泛素链编辑，精细控制T细胞抗原识别、受体信号转导、活化增殖和效应分化。通过调节T细胞受体、共刺激与细胞因子信号，以及关键转录因子和代谢调控分子的稳定性，E3与DUBs可影响T细胞活化阈值、无反应状态、存活及分化方向，共同构成维持T细胞稳态和外周免疫耐受的重要调控网络。该网络失衡可导致致炎性T细胞应答增强和调节性T细胞功能受损，削弱外周免疫耐受，并参与系统性红斑狼疮、类风湿关节炎和1型糖尿病等多种自身免疫病的发生和发展。系统归纳E3与DUBs调控T细胞命运的分子机制和关键信号通路，解析不同T细胞亚群中的底物谱、泛素链型偏好及其与代谢调控的交叉机制，有助于深化对泛素化维持T细胞稳态及参与自身免疫病发生和发展的认识，并为链型特异性和细胞类型选择性靶向策略的开发提供理论依据和转化方向。 蛋白质翻译后修饰是细胞整合外界刺激并调控功能状态的重要机制。其中，泛素化因具有可逆性强、链型多样和底物选择性高等特点，在免疫调控中发挥关键作用 [ 1- 2]。T细胞在激活、分化和效应功能执行过程中，对抗原信号的强度、持续时间及空间分布高度敏感，因此其命运依赖精确而动态的分子调控网络 [ 3]。 泛素-蛋白酶体系统(ubiquitin-proteasome system，UPS)广泛参与T细胞介导的免疫应答。该系统可通过调控T细胞受体(T cell receptor，TCR)信号复合体组装、关键转录因子稳定性及代谢适配过程，精细设定信号强度和持续时间，并为T细胞功能状态的形成提供重要分子基础 [ 3- 12]。基于此，本文系统综述UPS中的核心成分泛素-蛋白质连接酶(ubiquitin-protein ligase，E3)与去泛素化酶(deubiquitinases，DUB)在T细胞功能调控中的关键机制，并探讨其在自身免疫病中的作用与靶向干预潜力。 UPS在免疫调控中的功能定位 UPS是维持蛋白质稳态与信号精确性的核心调控网络 [ 6- 8, 10- 11]。该系统以泛素为修饰单元，通过泛素活化酶(ubiquitin-activating enzyme，E1)、泛素缀合酶(ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme，E2)和E3的级联反应，将泛素共价连接至底物蛋白的赖氨酸残基，形成单泛素化或不同链型的多聚泛素链 [ 13- 16]；DUBs则可去除或重塑这些泛素链，从而调控靶蛋白的降解周转、功能活性及亚细胞定位。E3与DUBs分别参与泛素信号的写入和去除/编辑，共同决定底物选择性、链型特征和信号输出，是泛素信号特异性的关键来源 [ 17]。在T细胞免疫调控中，UPS的作用并不局限于蛋白质降解，还可通过不同泛素链型传递特定信号 [ 15]。例如，K48连接型泛素链多介导蛋白酶体降解，用于终止或重置信号；K63连接型及其他非降解型泛素链则常作为信号支架，促进信号复合体装配和级联放大 [ 15, 18- 22]。 E3是泛素信号特异性的主要决定因素。其通过识别特定底物并催化不同链型的泛素化修饰，将TCR、共刺激和细胞因子信号转化为相对稳定的通路活化状态及细胞分化程序 [ 13, 16]。在T细胞中，免疫相关E3的功能大致可归纳为2类。第1类作用于TCR近端信号平台，通过调控信号复合体的组装、维持和拆解，设定T细胞激活阈值及信号持续时间。第2类直接调控谱系决定因子、共刺激分子及免疫突触相关组分的蛋白质周转，从而影响转录程序的维持或重置 [ 17, 23- 29]。因此，Casitas B系淋巴瘤蛋白b(Casitas B-lineage lymphoma-b，Cbl-b)、Itchy E3泛素蛋白连接酶(Itchy E3 ubiquitin protein ligase，Itch)、Roquin蛋白家族等E3在多种自身免疫病模型中反复被鉴定为关键调控节点。它们位于T细胞激活阈值和谱系分化程序的交汇处，其功能改变可削弱外周免疫耐受，并推动异常炎症反应发生。
